newsitem.title: USA: Wright Brothers number plates create turbulence.
newsitem.headline: Wright Brothers number plates create turbulence.

text.p: The legacy of pioneer aviators the Wright Brothers has hit a spot of turbulence.
The dispute between North Carolina, where Wilbur and Orville Wright made the first airplane flight in 1903, and Ohio, where they were born, has reached ground-level -- car bumpers to be exact.
North Carolina has for years decorated its vehicle number plates with the slogan: "First in Flight." Now Ohio plans to climb on board by introducing a vehicle tag saying "Birthplace of Aviation."
The Virginian-Pilot newspaper said state legislators, civic activists and media commentators have joined the dog fight, saying the Ohio slogan is inaccurate.

A meeting of the First Flight Centennial Commission in Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, on Wednesday brought together people from both sides and they agreed there was room for both slogans, the newspaper said.
But ordinary North Carolinians were still in a spin, it added.
"If Orville and Wilbur thought they could have flown in Ohio, they would have done it," said painter Gary Schaefer.
"The birthplace of aviation is right there in Kill Devil Hills."
